newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RICHEMONT FOLLOWS U.S. TOBACCO STOCKS UP.
newsitem.headline: RICHEMONT FOLLOWS U.S. TOBACCO STOCKS UP.

text.p: South African tobacco stock, Richemont Securities, on Thursday jumped on the same bandwagon as U.S. tobacco shares whose rally sparked Wall Street's latest rebound.
U.S. tobacco stocks were fuelled by news that tobacco executives there were negotiating to settle a massive litigation against the industry and that indications were a settlement could be reached.
Richemont shares were the second highest value traded on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange with more than 20 million rands worth trading.

The share opened more than two percent higher at 61 rand from its Wednesday close of 59.75 rand. By 100 GMT it had lost a little ground and was sitting at 60.50 rand, still 75 cents up. Volumes traded were 342,100 shares.
But local dealers added that the market had recently seen increased demand for rand hedge stocks and that this was propelling Richemont too.

"There has been good demand for Richemont and obviously the talks are helping them up. If there is a settlement it's great news for the industry but we've seen some big buying back of rand hedges lately," one dealer said.
Rembrandt , another local tobacco stock, was steady at 45.50 rand.

Rembrandt and Richemont merged their tobacco interests in October 1995 to form Luxembourg-incorporated company Rothmans International Holdings. Richemont owns two thirds of Rothmans International and Rembrandt one third.
The Dow surged 93 points to close at 6,679.8 points on Wednesday. Cigarette company Philip Morris Cos Inc led the advance, jumping 4-1/8 to 43-1/8 on the potential tobacco settlement.
